Neutral mode on.

**What RLS is**

Row Level Security (RLS) is a PostgreSQL feature. It lets you attach authorization rules to a table, and the database evaluates those rules itself. Supabase describes it as "granular authorization rules that run inside the database" [1].

**How it differs from a GRANT**

PostgreSQL runs two separate checks before a client touches a table [2]:

| Layer | Question it answers | Failure signal |
|---|---|---|
| GRANT | May this role run this operation on this table at all? | `42501` before any policy runs [2] |
| RLS policy | Which rows may that operation apply to? | Rows filtered out or rejected, depending on the operation |

**Policy clauses**

- `USING` filters existing rows. It applies to select, update and delete.
- `WITH CHECK` validates new or resulting rows. It applies to insert and update.
- If an update policy has no `WITH CHECK`, the `USING` expression covers both jobs [3].
- An `UPDATE` also needs a matching `SELECT` policy [3].

**Security points**

- A table in an exposed schema without RLS is readable and writable by any role with a grant on it [1].
- Adding policies does not remove existing grants. On projects that still auto-grant to `anon` and `authenticated`, you have to revoke them yourself [1][2].
- Once RLS is enabled, no data is accessible through the API with a publishable key until you create policies [3].
- The `service_role` Postgres role has `bypassrls`, so keep a secret key server-side only. If the request also carries a user's access token, the request runs under that user's policies [4].

Sources:
- [1] https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security.md#row-level-security (fetched 2026-10-21)
- [2] https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security.md#grants-and-policies (fetched 2026-10-21)
- [3] https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security.md#enable-rls-and-set-the-grants and https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security.md#write-a-policy-for-each-operation (fetched 2026-10-21)
- [4] https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security.md#bypassing-row-level-security (fetched 2026-10-21)
